title: Completion and continuous first-order deformation classes
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $A$ be a local ring obtained by localizing a finitely generated commutative $k$-algebra at a maximal ideal, and write $\mathfrak m$ for its maximal ideal. Let $\widehat A=\varprojlim_n A/\mathfrak m^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For an Artinian local $k$-algebra $R$ with residue field identified with $k$ (Artinian means descending chains of ideals stabilize), let $\mathcal D_A(R)$ be the groupoid of flat $R$-algebras $Q$ with an identified quotient $Q/\mathfrak m_RQ\cong A$; arrows preserve this quotient [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Put $\mathfrak n_Q$ equal to the inverse image of $\mathfrak m$ under $Q\to A$. Let $\mathcal D^{\mathrm{cont}}_{\widehat A}(R)$ be the groupoid of complete Noetherian local flat $R$-algebras with marked reduction $\widehat A$, with continuous marked isomorphisms. All topologies are maximal-ideal-adic. Then $Q\mapsto\widehat Q_{\mathfrak n_Q}$ is a natural functor $\mathcal D_A\to\mathcal D^{\mathrm{cont}}_{\widehat A}$; in particular $\widehat Q$ is $R$-flat and $\widehat Q\otimes_R k\cong\widehat A$.
Choose a presentation $P\twoheadrightarrow A$ with $P$ a localization of a finite polynomial $k$-algebra, and put $J=\ker(P\to A)$ and
$$C=[J/J^2\to\Omega^1_{P/k}\otimes_PA],\qquad \widehat C=C\otimes_A\widehat A,$$
in degrees $-1,0$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The second complex is the continuous conormal differential complex obtained by completing the presentation at the inverse image of $\mathfrak m$; continuous differentials mean the completion of the polynomial differential module, with its continuously extended derivation. Both complexes are independent of the chosen localized polynomial presentation up to canonical isomorphism in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. With the trivial deformation as origin, there are canonical $k$-linear identifications
$$\pi_0\mathcal D_A(k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(C,A[1]),\quad \pi_0\mathcal D^{\mathrm{cont}}_{\widehat A}(k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\widehat A)}(\widehat C,\widehat A[1]).$$
Under them, the tangent map of completion is extension of scalars along $A\to\widehat A$. Here $D(A)$ is the derived category of ordinary $A$-modules, and a module on the right is in degree zero before shifting. No separability or equality of the residue field of $A$ with $k$ is assumed. No assertion identifies ordinary differentials of $\widehat A/k$ with its continuous differentials.

source.place: Tag 0DYV (lemma-completion); defos.tex Tags 0GPZ (lemma-extensions-of-relative-ringed-spaces), 0GQ1 and 0GQ2, via completed polynomial presentations. restricted.tex Tag 0AJR (equation-NL) and Tag 0GAE (lemma-NL-up-to-homotopy), continuous presentation argument adapted to completion at a maximal ideal of a localized polynomial k-algebra; algebra.tex Tag 00MB (lemma-completion-flat). The continuous tangent comparison is this presentation-form consequence, not a verbatim assertion of 0DYV.

proof.text: A finitely generated algebra over $k$ is Noetherian, and localization preserves this, so $A$ is Noetherian. Apply the adic deformation functor theorem with $B=A$ and $J=\mathfrak m$. For a deformation $Q$, the ideal $\mathfrak m_RQ$ is nilpotent: the Artinian local maximal ideal is nilpotent. An element of $Q$ whose image is a unit in $A$ is a unit, since an inverse modulo a nilpotent ideal is corrected by a finite geometric series. Thus $Q$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n_Q$. Its completion is local by the local-completion theorem, and the deformation theorem supplies Noetherianity, flatness, the marked reduction and the natural base-change isomorphisms. These give exactly the claimed natural functor on groupoids.

source.place: Tag 0DYV (lemma-completion); algebra.tex Artinian and local completion results

proof.text: First choose the presentation local at the inverse image of $\mathfrak m$, so $P=k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]_{\mathfrak q}$. Such a presentation exists by lifting generators of the finite type algebra before localizing. The naive cotangent model identifies the conormal complex for any original localized polynomial presentation with $\tau_{\geq-1}L_{A/k}$, canonically and naturally. Thus replacing the presentation does not change its derived object. Both $P$ and $A$ are Noetherian by the two Noetherianity results in step 1. In particular $J$, $J^2$, $J/J^2$ and the differential module after tensoring with $A$ are finite modules. The polynomial calculus gives $\Omega^1_{P/k}=P^{\oplus r}$.

source.place: Tag 0GPU (remark-extensions-of-algebras); cotangent.tex Tag 08RB; localized polynomial presentation

proof.text: Put $S=\widehat P$, $B=\widehat A$ and $I=JS$. Completion of the quotient gives $B=S/I$. Complete the finite-module sequences $0\to J\to P\to A\to0$ and $0\to J^2\to J\to J/J^2\to0$. Exactness and the natural tensor comparison identify $I/I^2$ with $(J/J^2)\otimes_AB$: indeed the completed image of $J^2$ is $J^2S=(JS)^2$. The completed differential term is $B^{\oplus r}$. The polynomial calculus extends $d$ continuously, and on the dense representatives $j\in J$ the completed boundary is $[j]\mapsto\widehat d j$. Hence its complex is precisely $C\otimes_AB$. Every module map here is continuous since it preserves ideal powers; equality extends from representatives because finite modules over complete Noetherian rings are separated and complete.

source.place: Tag 0GPU, completed presentation calculation; algebra.tex Tags 00MA and 00MB

proof.text: The map $A\to B$ is flat, so ordinary tensoring carries the canonical quasi-isomorphisms between the algebraic presentation complexes to quasi-isomorphisms: tensor preserves the exact sequences defining cycles and boundaries. Consequently $\widehat C$ is independent of that presentation in $D(B)$. This proves the independence claimed in the statement, where the continuous complex is obtained by completing that presentation. It makes no comparison with the ordinary module $\Omega^1_{B/k}$.

Write $T=k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. For a flat $T$-algebra $E$ with reduction $H$, tensoring $0\to(\epsilon)\to T\to k\to0$ gives $\ker(E\to H)=\epsilon E\cong H$, via $\bar e\mapsto\epsilon e$. Conversely an extension $0\to H\xrightarrow{i}E\to H\to0$ of $k$-algebras with square-zero kernel becomes a $T$-algebra by $\epsilon\mapsto i(1)$. Multiplication then gives $\epsilon e=i(\bar e)$, so $\ker\epsilon=\operatorname{im}\epsilon=i(H)$. Choose a $k$-basis of $H$ and lifts to $E$. These lifts freely generate $E$ over $T$: reduction gives spanning modulo $i(H)$, and the same basis multiplied by $\epsilon$ spans $i(H)$; any linear relation vanishes first modulo $i(H)$ and then inside its identified copy of $H$. Thus $E$ is free and flat. The constructions are inverse on marked isomorphisms. For $H=B$ every such deformation is automatically complete Noetherian local by the adic deformation theorem, applied to the Noetherian $k$-algebra $B$ with its maximal ideal; $B$ is Noetherian by the same theorem applied in step 1 to the trivial deformation $A$ over $k$, whose completion is $B$, and $B$ is already complete. Marked isomorphisms are local, hence continuous.

source.place: Tag 0GPT (lemma-extensions-of-algebras), conversion between dual-number deformations and self-extensions

proof.text: For either $K=[N\xrightarrow{d}F]$ over a ring $H$, with $F$ finite free, or its displayed completed version, the boundary lemma gives $\operatorname{Hom}(F,H)\to\operatorname{Hom}(N,H)\xrightarrow{\partial}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(H)}(K,H[1])$, exact in the middle, with $\partial(\phi)=\phi[1]q$. It is also surjective: apply Hom-out-of-triangle exactness to the triangle $F[0]\to K\xrightarrow{q}N[1]\to F[1]$ and target $H[1]$. The restriction of any class to $F[0]$ is zero because $\operatorname{Ext}^1_H(F,H)=0$ by projectivity. It therefore factors through $q$. Thus $\partial$ identifies the cokernel of precomposition by $d$ with the required derived Hom. The boundary lemma makes this identification natural in chain maps and coefficient maps.

source.place: Tag 0GPU, displayed cokernel formula; derived.tex Tag 0149

proof.text: Apply step 5 with $H=A$ or $B$. In the first case lift $P\to A$ to $E$ by choosing lifts of the polynomial variables: all denominators remain units because their reductions are units. In the second case do this for $P\to B$ and use the polynomial calculus to extend to a continuous lift $a:S\to E$. In either case denote the presentation ring by $U$, its kernel by $V$ and its quotient by $H$. Restriction of $a$ to $V$ takes values in $i(H)$ and kills $V^2$; it gives an $H$-linear map $\phi:V/V^2\to H$. Two lifts differ by $iD$ with $D$ a $k$-derivation, because the kernel is square zero. In the completed case it is continuous; the polynomial calculus represents it by a linear map from the completed free differential module. In the ordinary case the same assertion follows by differentiating polynomials and $D(s^{-1})=-s^{-2}D(s)$. Thus changing the lift changes $\phi$ exactly by a map factoring through the conormal boundary.

source.place: Tag 0GPU (remark-extensions-of-algebras), lift and relation map; completed variant via 07ED

proof.text: Conversely, for any $\phi:V/V^2\to H$, form the ring $U\oplus H$ with $(u,b)(u',b')=(uu',\bar u b'+\bar u'b)$ and quotient it by the ideal $\{(v,-\phi([v])):v\in V\}$. It is an ideal since $\phi$ is linear and kills $V^2$. The quotient $E_\phi$ maps onto $H$ with kernel the injective copy $(0,H)$: an element in the kernel has $u\in V$ and equals $(0,b+\phi([u]))$, while a graph element with first coordinate zero has second coordinate zero. This kernel is square zero. Step 5 makes $E_\phi$ a flat dual-number deformation, and when $H=B$ the adic deformation theorem makes it complete Noetherian local. A lift $a:U\to E$ gives an isomorphism $E_\phi\to E$, $(u,b)\mapsto a(u)+i(b)$; it is bijective by the just displayed kernel calculation and surjectivity onto $H$. If $\phi'=\phi+D|_V$, the map $(u,b)\mapsto(u,b-D(u))$ induces $E_\phi\cong E_{\phi'}$. Conversely any marked isomorphism, compared with the canonical lifts, gives such a derivation. In the completed case all resulting isomorphisms are local and hence continuous. This proves bijectivity of the relation-map cokernel with deformation classes, with zero represented by the trivial deformation.

source.place: Tag 0GPU, explicit pushout of the conormal extension

proof.text: The cokernel description carries its usual $k$-vector-space structure. Fibre product of two square-zero extensions over $H$ pairs their relation maps $(\phi,\psi)$; pushout of the kernel along $(b,c)\mapsto b+c$ gives $\phi+\psi$. Pushout along $b\mapsto\lambda b$ gives $\lambda\phi$. These operations preserve the trivial origin and, in the completed case, are again complete deformations by step 5. The additive boundary map of step 6 respects scalars as composition is $k$-linear. Steps 6--8 therefore give the two stated canonical $k$-linear tangent identifications.

source.place: Tag 0GPU, addition and scalar multiplication on relation maps

proof.text: Finally let $a:P\to E$ represent an algebraic deformation class by $\phi:J/J^2\to A$. The map into $\widehat E$ extends to $\widehat a:S\to\widehat E$. Completing $0\to A\xrightarrow{i}E\to A\to0$ as a sequence of finite $E$-modules is exact, and identifies its kernel with $\widehat A=B$; the topology on $A$ induced by the maximal ideal of $E$ is exactly the $\mathfrak m$-adic topology. For $j\in J$ one has $\widehat a(j)=i(\phi([j]))$ in that completed kernel. By the natural finite-module tensor comparison the continuous relation map is consequently $\widehat\phi:I/I^2\to B$, with $\widehat\phi([j]\otimes b)=b\phi([j])$. The same formula extends the maps factoring through differentials. Passing to cokernels and then through the boundary map of step 6 is exactly extension of scalars along $A\to B$: since $A\to B$ is flat, $-\otimes_AB$ is an exact functor of module categories, so it preserves quasi-isomorphisms, induces $D(A)\to D(B)$ commuting with $[1]$, and sends the quotient chain map $q:C\to(J/J^2)[1]$ to the quotient chain map of $\widehat C$ and $\phi[1]$ to $(\phi\otimes_AB)[1]$, with $A\otimes_AB=B$; hence it sends $\partial_A(\phi)=\phi[1]q$ to $\partial_B(\widehat\phi)$. Hence it is the tangent map of the completion functor. This calculation uses no coefficient-field section and remains valid for inseparable residue extensions.
